newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa platinum stocks fall as metal below $400.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa platinum stocks fall as metal below $400.

text.p: South African platinum stocks were under pressure in early dealings on Wednesday after the white metal price dipped below $400 and fears that Russia may start exporting stocks later this year weighed.
By 0744 GMT the Johannesburg Stock Exchange platinum index was off almost 1.9 percent or 96.7 points at 5,007.1.
"The shares are down as the platinum dollar price is under pressure...There is also concern that Russia may start exporting later this year," one dealer said.
Platinum was last bid at $397 from a New York close of $402.50/405.50.
Amongst platinum shares Rusplats was down 175 cents to 74.50 rand, Lebowa Platinum fell 35 cents to 425 cents and Potgieterust Platinum slid 70 cents to 30.30 rand.
Dealers said a renewed slide in the bullion price, which early on Wednesday slid to around the $315 level after a mini-rally above $320 on Tuesday, was also hurting platinum stocks.
"Stocks are being marked down on sentiment about golds. But ultimately if you want to be in the metals market, platinum is a far better place to be than gold," a dealer said.
